# #192 — Feature: cheaper recall of large entries — condensed retrieval + dream-driven decomposition

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-06-21T20:31:16Z
Updated: 2026-07-06T04:25:16Z
Closed: 2026-07-06T04:25:16Z

---

Two complementary capabilities for making recall of large entries cheap. Not a blocker for current work; captured as a feature gap. **Verified from source 2026-06-21.**

## Part A — No compact-retrieval mode (verified gap)

`get_entry` returns full stored content (`src/tools/get-entry.ts`: `SELECT <all columns> ... WHERE id = $1` → `JSON.stringify(rows[0])`; the column set includes full text fields per `src/table-projections.ts`). `brain_answer` pulls full rows and only truncates for the 500-char citation display (`src/tools/brain-answer.ts` `excerptFor` → `.slice(0, 500)`); `content_preview` is a query-time concat of full fields, not a stored condensed column. Tiering (hot/warm/cold) affects ranking, not payload size.

Net: there is no way to store a rich entry but recall a condensed form — the only lever is "store small + retrieve few." Every UUID fetch pays the full token cost of that entry.

*Possible direction:* a `get_entry` projection param returning a stored/computed `summary`, a real condensed-render retrieval mode distinct from the display-only excerpt, or a documented "by design — chunk small" stance if compact recall is explicitly out of scope.

## Part B — Dream-driven decomposition (the preferred fix)

Extend the dream cycle (which already promotes/demotes tiers) to detect oversized entries and refactor them into properly-structured, smaller, independently-retrievable entries with `[[links]]` back to the original/related context. This reduces the *need* for Part A by keeping entries naturally small and cheaply consumable — working with OB's actual architecture (small entries + tiering + links) instead of bolting on a retrieval-time compression mode.

## Why P1

Wanted fairly soon, but **sequenced after** the repo-enforcement recall pattern is verified to work. The "always-known basics" direct-UUID-fetch design depends on cheap recall, so this becomes a priority right after that proof.
